# Temple Scroll Column 56 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 56 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**56:1** Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out grain.

**56:2** If brothers are living together and one of them dies without leaving a son, his widow must not marry an outsider. Instead, her brother-in-law must marry her and fulfill his obligation as her husband's brother.

**56:3** The first son she bears will be considered the legal heir of the dead brother, so that his name will not die out in Israel.

**56:4** But if the man refuses to marry his brother's widow, she must go to the town gate and tell the elders: My brother-in-law refuses to preserve his brother's name in Israel. He will not fulfill his obligation to me.

**56:5** The city elders shall call him in and talk to him. If he still insists, saying: I do not want to marry her —

**56:6** then the widow must go up to him in front of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and announce: This is what happens to the man who refuses to continue his brother's family line!

**56:7** From then on, his family will be known in Israel as "the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off."

**56:8** If two men are fighting and the wife of one of them steps in to rescue her husband from the man hitting him, and she reaches out and grabs the other man's genitals —

**56:9** you must cut off her hand. Show no mercy.

**56:10** Do not carry two sets of weights in your bag — one heavy, one light.

**56:11** Do not keep two different measuring containers in your house — one large, one small.

**56:12** Use only accurate and honest weights and measures, so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you.

**56:13** For the LORD your God detests anyone who deals dishonestly.

**56:14** When you enter the land I am giving you and take possession of it and settle there, and you decide: I want a king to rule over me, like the nations around me —

**56:15** you must be sure to appoint the king I choose for you. He must be one of your own people; do not place a foreigner over you who is not one of your own.

**56:16** The king must not build up a large stable of horses for himself, and he must never send people back to Egypt to get more horses, for I have told you: You are never to go back that way again.

**56:17** He must not take many wives, or his heart will be led astray. He must not accumulate large amounts of silver and gold.

**56:18** When he takes the throne, a copy of this Torah must be written for him on a scroll, taken from the one kept by the priests.

**56:19** He must keep it with him and read it every day of his life, so that he will learn to revere the LORD his God by faithfully obeying every word of this Torah and these regulations,

**56:20** so that he will not consider himself better than his fellow Israelites, and will not turn from these commands in any way. Then he and his descendants will reign for a long time over Israel.

**56:21** He must not [...] the inheritance of any tribe, for each tribe must retain its own inheritance.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 56 covers Deuteronomy 25:4-17:20, culminating in the Law of the King. The levirate obligation is explained in modern family law terms. The Law of the King (56:14-21) is presented with the distinctive divine first-person voice. "Build up a large stable" for multiplying horses — making the military accumulation concern vivid.*
